svg.aria-label: so sessions are built by comparing CONSECUTIVE event times
svg.text: Three window shapes through one assigner
fixed 1 window · sliding 2 windows · session bounds decided by the data
2 // Two of an event's five fields are CLOCKS, which ch01 established:
3 // et = event time, when it happened · pt = processing time, when we saw it
4 // v = the value being summed · key = whose activity this is
5 type Event { id, key, et, pt, v }
6 // primitive: EVENTS — the book's 9 events, in PROCESSING order (tools/stream_seed.js).
7 // EVENTS[7] = (id 7, key "b", et 50, pt 280, v 4) <- the straggler
8 // primitive: NONE — no value. Distinct from a value of 0.
9 // primitive: GAP — the session gap: silence longer than this ends a session. GAP = 120
10 // primitive: WIN — the fixed window width. WIN = 120
11 // primitive: LAG — the watermark's assumed worst-case skew. LAG = 60
12 // primitive: KEYS — the keys sessions are tracked per. KEYS = ["a", "b"]
13 // primitive: sum(ids) — total v over those event ids.
15 // primitive: append(xs, x) — xs with x added at the end. append([1], 2) = [1,2]
16 // primitive: sortByEt(es) — es in ascending event-time order.
18 // primitive: watermarkAfter(i) — highest event time through i, minus LAG.
23 // primitive: PERIOD — how often a sliding window starts. PERIOD = 60
24 // primitive: winOf(et) — the START of the fixed window holding et.
26 // primitive: slidingStarts(et) — EVERY sliding window start covering et.
29 // function: assign(e, shape) — the windows one event belongs to. Fixed and
30 // sliding answer from e.et alone; a session cannot be answered yet at all.
33 // assign(EVENTS[4], "session") = NONE (the bounds depend on events not yet seen)
40 // function: sessionize(key, gap) — build that key's sessions in EVENT-time order.
59 // function: totalAcross(shape) — add up every window's sum, to show which
60 // shapes partition event time and which overlap.
64 for (e in EVENTS) { t = t + e.v * len(assign(e, shape)) }
68 // function: main() — THE CALLER: three shapes, and two gaps.
Step 3/0 — so sessions are built by comparing CONSECUTIVE event times
The event at et 130 is compared against `last.end` = 3: the difference is 127, which exceeds GAP = 120, so the `if` fails and the next line starts a new session.
One subtraction and one comparison decide every session boundary in the book.
